extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent classification specialists, patent information professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the International Patent Classification (IPC) rules to determine appropriate classification places, indexing codes, and presentation of classification symbols for patent documents at various publication/examination stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place selection for processes, apparatus and products
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns a process, classify in the place for the process. When such a place does not exist, the making or treatment of products is classified in the place for the apparatus performing the process. If no place exists for the manufacture of a product, the manufacturing apparatus or process is classified in the place covering the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the place that best represents the technical subject; fall back to the apparatus place for process-derived products and to the product place for apparatus/process when no specific manufacture place exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles of manufacture classification
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject of the invention concerns an article, it is classified in the place for the article. If no place exists for the article itself, it is classified in the appropriate function-oriented place (i.e., according to the function performed by the article) or, if this is not possible, according to the field of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a glue-dispenser specially adapted for bookbinding is classified in B42C 9/00 ('Applying glue peculiar to bookbinding') — function-oriented classification when a specific article place is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of multistep processes and industrial plants
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention concerns a multistep process or an industrial plant that consists of a combination of process steps or apparatus, it is classified as a whole in a place provided for such combination. If no such place exists, it is classified in the place for the product obtained by the process or plant. Elements of the combination (individual steps or machines) are also separately classified when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a group for the combination; still classify novel subelements separately as invention information when they are novel and unobvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of details and constructional parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Details or parts only applicable to, or specially adapted for, one kind of subject matter are classified in the details places of this kind of subject matter, if such places exist; if not, they are classified in the place for the subject matter in question. Details or parts applicable to more than one kind are classified in the details places of more general nature if such places exist; if not, they are classified according to all of the kinds of subject matter to which they explicitly apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific 'details' groups exist, use them; otherwise use the main subject places or multiple places corresponding to each applicable subject matter (example: umbrella details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of fully identified compounds from general chemical formulae (Step 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification should be given to all 'fully identified' compounds that are novel and unobvious if they are (i) specifically claimed as such or in a composition, (ii) products of a claimed process, or (iii) derivatives of either of these. A compound is considered 'fully identified' where the structure is given by exact chemical name or formula, or can be deduced from its preparation from specified reactants (not more than one of which is selected from a list of alternatives), and the compound is characterised by a physical property or its preparation is described in a worked example giving practical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat empirically-identified-only compounds as 'fully identified'. Classify all qualifying fully-identified, novel, unobvious compounds into the most specific groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification when no fully identified compounds are disclosed (Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no 'fully identified' compounds are disclosed (e.g., computer-generated models without experiments), classification should only be given to compounds with exact chemical name or developed chemical formula. Classification should be limited to a single or a very small number of groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit classification breadth for speculative or unverified compound disclosures; avoid proliferating classification symbols when identity is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification when only a general Markush formula is disclosed (Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When only the general Markush formula is disclosed, classification is made in the most specific group(s) that cover(s) all or most of the potential embodiments. Classification should be limited to a single or a very small number of groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the smallest set of groups that meaningfully cover the formula's embodiments to avoid excessive symbol counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-obligatory classification for other compounds from general formulae (Step 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to obligatory classification, non-obligatory classification may be made when other compounds within the scope of the general formula, or compounds derived directly from computer-generated models, are of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discretionary classification when specific additional members are of search interest, but distinguish these from obligatory invention information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting number of classification symbols for large sets of compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When classification of all 'fully identified' compounds into their most specific classification places would lead to a high number of classification symbols (for example, more than twenty), the classifier may reduce the number of symbols. This may only be done when classification of the 'fully identified' compounds would lead to the assigning of a large number of subgroups under a single group at the next hierarchically higher level. Classification of these compounds may then be made in the higher group only. Otherwise, classification of the compounds is made in all of the more specific subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only aggregate to a higher group to prevent unwieldy symbol proliferation that would not aid searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of combinatorial libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections presented as 'libraries' (many compounds, biological entities or substances) should have only the individual members which are 'fully identified' obligatorily classified into the groups that most specifically provide for them. The library as a whole is classified in an appropriate group in subclass C40B. Non-obligatory classifications may be made for other members of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the library as an entity in C40B and classify only fully-identified individual members into specific groups unless additional members warrant discretionary classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple classification: when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple classification is necessary when the invention information relates to two or more inventive things that can each be classified in different groups (for example, alternative embodiments, or both a product and a process for its production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each inventive thing (distinct claims, alternatives, categories) and assign separate classification symbols where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple classification for different aspects of a single inventive thing
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple classification should also be made when a single inventive thing is characterised by different aspects that are covered in different groups (e.g., construction, material, means for control) or is of interest both in a function-oriented place and an application-oriented place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply several symbols to capture distinct searchable aspects; consider indexing in combination with classification to indicate additional searchable facets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of hybrid systems and indexing schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid systems combine a classification scheme and associated complementary indexing scheme. When classifying within a hybrid system, assign all classification symbols appropriate to the technical subjects first, then add any appropriate indexing codes from associated indexing schemes if they identify elements useful for search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes are applied only in association with classification symbols and are indicated by notes where applicable; use indexing for aspects not covered by classification places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing codes: format and hierarchical use
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing codes have a format similar to classification symbols. In indexing schemes, the hierarchically higher group is only to be used in a residual manner to record a specific feature not provided for in any of its subdivisions. When indexing two or more elements, for each element the hierarchically lowest indexing group which provides for this element should be applied. Indexing should not be made in main groups of very wide or general scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor the most specific indexing group available; avoid using overly general indexing groups that are unhelpful for searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of indexing codes for search usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing codes may be applied when it is desirable for search purposes to identify elements of information about a technical subject of the invention already classified as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply indexing where it materially improves retrieval; example provided illustrating avoiding a too-general indexing code that gives no useful search information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligatory classification (invention information) per Article 4(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an obligation to allot the classification symbols that represent invention information; competent authorities shall indicate 'the complete symbols of the Classification applied to the invention to which the patent document relates'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always assign classification symbols representing invention information; this is mandatory regardless of discretionary indexing or additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-obligatory classification and indexing for additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable that additional information is classified or indexed, when it is useful for search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat additional (non-invention) information as discretionary for classification or indexing if it enhances searchability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of granted patents (post-search/examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: All subject matter covered by the claims of a patent document must be classified as invention information along with any novel and unobvious constituents or components (subcombinations) of the claimed subject matter. Classification should be based on the subject matter of each claim as a whole and on each inventive embodiment within a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both whole-claim subject matter and separately novel subcombinations in invention information classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of unclaimed novel/unobvious disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any unclaimed subject matter in the disclosure that is novel and unobvious must also be classified as invention information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not limit classification solely to claims — novel/unobvious material in the description should be classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of searched but unexamined patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: All claimed subject matter that appears to be novel and unobvious in view of the search results must be classified as invention information along with any novel and unobvious constituents or components of the claimed subject matter. Any unclaimed subject matter that appears novel and unobvious by the search results must also be classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on search results to determine which claim-elements and unclaimed disclosures are treated as invention information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of unsearched patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: All claimed subject matter that is potentially novel and unobvious in the opinion of the classifier who is an expert in the art must be classified as invention information along with any potentially novel and unobvious constituents or components. For classifiers who are not experts in the relevant technical field, all the claims must be used for determining the subject matter to be classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert judgment guides classification for unsearched docs; non-experts should conservatively consider all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: General observation: separately classify all inventive things
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents should not be classified as a single entity; all different inventive things, claimed or disclosed within the patent document, should be identified and separately classified. If two or more inventive things in a document separately are covered by the same group, the classification symbol of that group is allotted only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify different inventive objects (different claims, alternatives, categories) and assign separate symbols; avoid duplicate symbols for the same group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum assignment when no invention information found
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a classifier determines that no invention information is present within a patent document, at least one classification symbol must still be assigned to the patent document as an invention information symbol, based on that portion of the total disclosure that the classifier determines as most useful for search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always assign at least one invention-information symbol even if no clear invention is found, choosing the part most useful for searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and revision of classifications to minimise unnecessary symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize potentially unnecessary classification symbols, the classification of a previously published application may be reviewed when the application is granted, searched, evaluated or abandoned, in order to confirm or alter its classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-classify where appropriate during the prosecution lifecycle to avoid overclassification; note some offices classify only once and do not revise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a subclass: hierarchical and alternative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the appropriate subclass, identify the relevant section, subsection and class, then the subclass which most satisfactorily covers the subject. Alternative methods include using an alphabetical Catchword Index, text searching in the IPC, or reviewing classification symbols of related patent documents, but always verify scope against hierarchically superior places and local classification rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hierarchical approach as default but apply catchword/text-search/statistical review to speed selection; verify the chosen place's scope with notes and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a group: check applicable general and special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After selecting a subclass, determine which of the three general classification rules (common rule, first place priority rule, last place priority rule) is used in the selected subclass and whether any special classification rules are applied; then follow the procedure appropriate to that rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rules may vary between parts of a subclass; always check for notes indicating which rule applies before choosing groups or subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common rule (default) for group selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The common rule is the 'default' classification rule in the IPC: no general priority rules apply and classification should be made in all appropriate places. After selecting a subclass, review all main groups and subgroups to identify which provide for the subject; subject matter relating to a combination is primarily classified in a group that provides for the combination as a whole, otherwise classify according to subcombinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply multiple classification where multiple groups match; prioritize combination groups when present, and classify subcombinations separately when novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: First place priority rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In areas where the first place priority rule applies, classification is made in the first appropriate place at each hierarchical level (in the absence of an indication to the contrary). The procedure is: (a) determine the first main group in the subclass which provides at least in part for the subject; (b) determine, under this main group, the first one-dot subgroup which provides at least in part for the subject; (c) repeat to the deepest appropriate subgroup level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ordered sequence of groups (more specialised to less) to locate the first matching place at each level; apply the rule separately to each particular technical subject disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last place priority rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In areas where the last place priority rule applies, classification is made in the last appropriate place at each hierarchical level. The procedure mirrors the first place rule but selects the last matching main group and last one-dot subgroup at each level, repeated to the deepest appropriate subgroup level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when subclass notes indicate last place priority; apply separately for each disclosed technical subject and for subcombinations as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special classification rules override general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In a limited number of places, special classification rules are used which override the general classification rules. Wherever special rules are used, they are clearly specified in notes at the places concerned (example: C08L Note 2(b): compositions classified according to the macromolecular constituent present in the highest proportion; if equal, classify according to each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check notes at subclass/group titles for special rules and follow them instead of common/priority rules when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation order and formatting of classification symbols and indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The order is: (a) classification symbols representing invention information, with the symbol which most adequately represents the invention listed first; (b) classification symbols representing additional information; (c) indexing codes. Symbols and codes are presented in tabular form with one symbol/code per line; when classifying in the full IPC, put version indicators in round brackets after symbols; invention information symbols printed/displayed in bold, additional information in regular font; when classifying in main groups only, use regular font, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified order and font conventions (bold/italics/version indicators) and layout rules (columns read top-down then next column) for consistent presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special residual classification places (99Z 99/00 and 99/00)
rubrics_metrics.description: When invention information is not adequately covered by any subclasses of the most appropriate section, classify in the special residual main group of that section designated '99Z 99/00'. When invention information is covered by a subclass but not by any of its groups with specific titles, classify in a residual main group of that subclass designated '99/00' placed at the end of the subclass scheme. Residual groups have standard notes and should be used only after thoroughly considering other subclasses or main groups. Combinations of subject matter covered by two or more different main groups should not be classified in a residual main group unless indicated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use residual places as a last resort; respect the standard note and search for better-fitting specific places before assigning residual symbols.
